events.text: A hunter in the tavern swears the beasts in the hills have gone strange: wolves walking in pairs, deer standing on the ridges at dusk, all facing east. 'The valley is waking,' an old woman says from the corner. 'The Valley of a Hundred Beasts. It opens every twelve years, and the beasts always know first.'

effects.log: She tells you of the white ape that guards it, the clan that raised it, and the governor who burned them. By the end the whole tavern has gone quiet to listen.
If the beasts are getting ready, so can you. You are in the practice yard before dawn the next day.

variants: The shepherds bring their flocks down early this year. Up in the hills the wolves go in pairs and the deer stand on the ridges at dusk, all looking east. The old people know the sign: the Valley of a Hundred Beasts is waking.

Crows by the thousand fly east every evening, and not one comes back to roost. In the villages they say the beasts always know first: the Valley of a Hundred Beasts opens once in twelve years, and its time is near.

The hunters come home empty-handed: every beast in the hills is standing still at dusk, facing east. "The Valley of a Hundred Beasts," says an old woman, "opens every twelve years, and the beasts always know first."

events.text: A wandering scholar at a market stall is selling copies of a badly drawn map: a mountain shoulder, roofless halls, a long stair. 'The Ruins of the Nameless Sect,' he says. 'They come back soon. Nobody knows what the sect was called. Nobody knows why it burned its own name.'

effects.log: On the back, in faded ink, someone has written: "Do not fight in the library."
"Because a name burned on purpose is a secret kept on purpose," he says, and taps the map. "And secrets keep."

variants: A pedlar is selling scraps of burnt silk, sworn to have blown down from the hills: pieces of banners with the name cut out of every one. The Ruins of the Nameless Sect are coming back, says the pedlar, and nobody knows what they burned.

Maps of the Ruins of the Nameless Sect are selling in the market again: a mountain shoulder, roofless halls, a long stair. The ruins are coming back, people say, and nobody knows the name they burned.

events.text: In the villages, households have started setting out jars of water on their doorsteps at night. It is the old custom, someone explains: before the Spirit Spring opens, the moon in a jar of water shines a little brighter. Every jar on your street is shining.

choices.text: Set out a jar of your own

effects.log: In the morning the water in it tastes faintly of silver. You drink it before anyone can tell you not to.
An old woman tells you about the jade carp, the moon-watching nuns, and the cup that was never turned over.

variants: At night every doorstep on your street holds a jar of water, the old custom, and every jar holds a moon a little brighter than the one in the sky. The Spirit Spring will open soon. The grandmothers are sure of it.
The old women of the village have begun to set water jars on their doorsteps again, and at night the moon in every jar is a little too bright. The Spirit Spring is close to opening.

events.text: Treasure hunters are flooding the river towns, buying shovels and rope and maps of bandit tunnels at outrageous prices. The Bandit King's Vault opens soon, and every one of them is sure they will find the real gold among the hundred chests of rocks. The shopkeepers are getting richer than any of them will.

effects.log: "Patience," you tell them, which is all you know. They pay you anyway.
You leave them to their maps. Let the fools dig first.

variants: Every river town is full of strangers with new shovels. Rope sells by the inch, and a map of the bandit tunnels costs more than a horse. The Bandit King's Vault opens soon, and each of them knows the real gold is in the one chest the others will miss.

The ferrymen have doubled their fares: half the province wants to cross the river before the Bandit King's Vault opens. A hundred chests of rocks, the old story goes, and one of gold. Nobody on the ferry thinks the rocks are meant for them.

A boy in the market is selling "the Bandit King's own key", a rusty thing on a string, for the price of a cow. The stall has sold nine today. The Vault opens soon, and sense has gone out of the river towns with the tide.

events.text: A blind flute player in the market has begun playing a new tune: three notes, a pause, three notes, over and over. People stop to listen without knowing why. 'The bamboo is waking,' he says when you drop a coin in his bowl. 'The Labyrinth opens soon. I can hear its wind already.'

effects.log: You hum it all the way home. Your feet keep time with it in a pattern you do not recognise.
He only smiles, and plays it again, a little louder.

variants: Wind moves in the bamboo along the river road on days when there is no wind, three rustles, a pause, three more. A woodcutter makes the old sign and turns home. The Bamboo Labyrinth is breathing again.

Children in the lanes have a new clapping game, three claps, a stop, three claps, and none of them can say where they learned it. The old flute player smiles at it: the Labyrinth is near, and the bamboo is calling.

events.text: Ghost lights have been seen on the old plain where nothing grows: rows of them, in ranks, marching. Farmers bar their doors. The sects send scouts, and the scouts come back pale. Everyone knows what it means. The Ancient Battlefield is stirring, and it opens only once in sixty years.

effects.log: From a hilltop you watch them march, rank after rank, in perfect silence, toward a war three thousand years over.
Whatever is marching out there, it will not find you blunt.

events.text: Fishermen on the great lake are pulling strange things up in their nets: tiles of green glaze, a bronze bell the size of a fist, a jade hairpin. The water has turned warm, and at night, some swear, there are lights far down. The Sunken Palace is rising. It opens once in sixty years.

effects.log: It is cold in your hand, colder than jade should be, and smells of deep water.
Far out, for a moment, a roof of green tiles catches the moon, and is gone.

events.text: Herb sellers have doubled their prices and the doctors are buying anyway. Every herb in the market smells stronger, greener; even common mint makes your eyes water. 'The Herb Valley,' the herbalists say. 'It is breathing again. Sixty years since it last opened.'

effects.log: You brew it that night. Your meridians hum like a plucked string until morning.
Nobody will speak of it above a whisper. The ginseng, the serpent, sixty years: the words go round the market like a cold wind.

events.text: A mountain far to the west has begun to glow at night, faintly, from inside, like a lantern under a cloth. Monks fast and pray. Masters go into seclusion. The Fallen Immortal's Cave is opening, once in sixty years, and whatever fell there long ago is said to wait for a worthy heir.

effects.log: A month of silence. You come out with clearer eyes and no worthier than before, but readier.
It pulses, slowly, like something asleep and dreaming.

events.text: In the north, swords have begun to hum in their scabbards: every blade in every armoury, a thin low note, all on the same pitch. Smiths are terrified. Old swordsmen are delighted. 'The Frozen Sword Tomb is calling,' they say. 'The swords know it is almost time.'

effects.log: It hums too, very faintly, when you hold it to your ear. You did not know it had a voice.
The humming stops. The silence is somehow worse.

events.text: People have started seeing things in still water: their reflection a breath too late, or smiling when they are not. Mirrors crack in the night. The fortune-tellers have all gone quiet. Only the oldest says it aloud: the Mirror Realm is about to open, and it shows everyone the face they do not want to see.

choices.text: Look into a basin of water

effects.log: Your reflection looks back, a moment late. You stare at it until it catches up.

choices.text: Cover the mirrors in your room

effects.log: You hang cloth over every one. You sleep better, and feel a little foolish.

events.text: The older children in the lane talk of nothing but {sr_next}, which opens soon. You listen from the edge of their game. The barrier, they say, turns back anyone under twelve. You count the years on your fingers, and then count them again.

effects.log: You swing a stick at the woodpile until your arms ache. When the time comes, you will be ready.
They tell you about beasts and ghosts and treasure, most of it invented. You believe every word.

events.text: Word comes that {sr_next} will open soon, and the young fighters in the region talk of nothing else. You remember being that young. But the barrier of a minor realm throws back anyone above First-Rate, and you are long past it. Whatever waits in there belongs to someone younger now, unless you send someone.

effects.log: You find yourself watching the young faces around you, measuring them.

choices.text: Tell the young ones what you know

effects.log: They gather round like children at a storyteller's mat. A few of them will remember your advice at the right moment.

variants: The young fighters of the region talk of one thing: {sr_next} is about to open. You were that young once. The barrier of a minor realm will not let anyone past First-Rate through, and whatever waits there belongs to someone younger, unless you send one.

Rumour runs through every teahouse: {sr_next} opens soon. The barrier of a minor realm throws back anyone above First-Rate, and you are far beyond that now. If anyone of yours is to go in, you will have to choose them.

{sr_next} will open soon, and the young of the region can talk of nothing else. Its barrier turns back anyone above First-Rate, and you are long past that. What waits inside belongs to someone younger, unless you send one.

events.text: The great sects are already choosing their parties for {sr_next}, once in sixty years, and every Transcendent in the land is counting the days. Not you. You have climbed past the barrier's limit, and the realm will throw you back like a stone off a wall. It is a strange grief, to be too strong for a door.

choices.text: Choose who to send in your place

effects.log: You make a list of names, and cross most of them out, and look a long time at the rest.
The world has other doors. You have walked through most of them.

events.text: The notice goes up on the board: {sr_next} opens soon, and the elders will choose a party to send in. Every disciple in the yard reads it twice. Overnight the practice yard is full before dawn, and nobody is friendly any more.

effects.log: You are first in the yard and last out of it. The elders notice. So does everyone else.

choices.text: Make friends with the elders' favourites

effects.log: A word here, a shared meal there. Parties are chosen by people, after all.
You keep your own pace. Whoever goes in, the mountain will still be here.

events.text: The sect master announces it at the morning assembly, and the hall goes silent: {sr_next}, the great one, opens soon, and the sect will send its best. Once in sixty years. Old disciples who missed the last one weep openly. Young ones stare at each other, measuring.

effects.log: The sect master looks at you for a long moment and nods once. It is not a promise. It is not a no.

choices.text: Find an old disciple who went in last time

effects.log: The old disciple talks for an hour and tells you almost nothing, and the nothing is very useful.

events.text: Someone at the inn mentions {sr_next}, and the whole table turns to look at you. You have been inside a secret realm in this life and come out alive. They want to know what it is like.

effects.log: It is frightening and beautiful and you nearly died. They listen as if you were telling a legend.
The ape grows bigger, the ghosts fiercer, the treasure brighter. You are very popular by the end of the evening.

events.text: The parties gather at the barrier of {sr_realm} in their colours, banners up, checking each other's gear. Names are called. Yours is not among them. You stand at the edge of the crowd and watch the chosen walk into the mist, and the barrier closes behind them like water.

choices.text: Look for a crack in the barrier

effects.log: You walk its edge slowly, the way a thief walks a wall. There are always cracks.
Next time they will call your name. You decide it right there.
It goes down hard, and stays down. You breathe until it settles.

events.text: Outside {sr_realm}, the sellers of rope and bandages are doing a roaring trade, and so are the sellers of maps, most of them fake. A whole second crowd waits at the gate: the ones nobody chose. Some will sneak in. Most will wait all season to hear who came out.

effects.log: It is probably fake. It still makes you feel better.

choices.text: Talk to the others who were left out

effects.log: Half of them are planning to sneak in. The other half are planning to be angry about it for years.

events.text: The elders of your sect read the names for {sr_realm} from a scroll in the main hall. They are good names, strong ones, and every one belongs to someone the elders like. When the scroll is rolled up, a few faces turn to you, some with pity, some with satisfaction. Nobody says a word.

choices.text: Go to the elders and ask why

ok.log: The second elder hears you out and grunts. "Next time," the elder says, and writes something down.

fail.log: "Because we chose," says the first elder, and that is all you get.

effects.log: You shake every hand. Some of them feel guilty. That is worth something.
There is more than one way through a barrier. You start thinking about the cracks.

events.text: Your sect passes over you for {sr_realm} kindly, which is worse. 'At your age,' the sect master says, 'there is nothing left to prove.' The young ones chosen instead are half your age and have a quarter of your scars.

effects.log: You give the chosen the best of what you know. One of them listens properly, and that one comes back.
"Nothing to prove," you say, "is not the same as nothing to find." The sect master does not answer.

events.text: No sect, no banner, no party: at the gate of {sr_realm} the sect guards look straight through you. A wanderer goes where the wind blows, one of them says, but the wind does not blow through a sealed barrier.

effects.log: You have always found other ways. There is no reason this should be different.
You watch the banners pass and learn more about who hates whom than a year of tavern gossip would teach.

events.text: You remember {sr_realm}. The soul does, at least: the smell of it, the weight of the air. The party that goes in without you does not know that you know a road into it better than any of its chosen. It is a strange thing, to be left behind by people who would need you.

choices.text: Go in by your own road

effects.log: Let them have the front gate. You know where the barrier is thin.

choices.text: Tell one of the chosen a little

effects.log: You take a nervous young fighter aside and say which way to turn at the first fork. They stare at you as if you were a ghost.

events.text: The great sects choose their parties for {sr_realm} at a gathering with music and speeches, and heralds read out the list. It opens once in sixty years: for most people, once in a lifetime. Your name is not on the list. The music goes on anyway.

choices.text: Swear to get in, whatever it costs

effects.log: Once in a lifetime is not a door you let close in your face.
Once in a lifetime. Perhaps you will have more than one. Perhaps the soul already has.

events.text: {npc} walks beside you through {sr_realm}, close enough that your shoulders brush in the narrow places. Neither of you says much. At a fork {he} stops and looks at you, and you realise {he} has been waiting all day for you to choose the way, because {he} trusts you to.

mem.note: chose the road for us in the secret realm, and chose well

effects.log: You pick the left. It is the right way. {npc} lets out a breath {he} did not know {he} was holding.

mem.note: asked me to choose the road in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} picks the right, surprised to be asked. It is the longer way, and the prettier one.

events.text: Halfway through {sr_realm}, {npc} slips into a ravine to the waist and you grab {his} wrist without thinking. For a moment {his} whole weight hangs on your arm. Then you haul, and {he} scrambles up, and the two of you sit on the edge breathing hard and laughing like fools.

mem.note: caught me at the edge of a ravine in the secret realm

effects.log: You laugh until your ribs hurt. {He} keeps hold of your sleeve for the rest of the morning and pretends not to.

mem.note: pulled me out of a ravine in the secret realm, and scolded me for it

effects.log: {He} makes a face at you, and watches {his} step. The next ravine, {he} catches you.

events.text: {npc} has a habit, you discover inside {sr_realm}, of humming when frightened. {He} hums all the way through the darkest stretch of the road, badly off key, and does not seem to know {he} is doing it.

mem.note: hummed with me in the dark of the secret realm

effects.log: After a while you are both humming, badly, and the dark is a great deal less dark.

mem.note: never mentioned my humming in the dark

effects.log: You never mention it. Years later {he} will thank you for that, and you will pretend not to know what for.

events.text: Night falls inside {sr_realm} with no moon, and you and {npc} keep watch by turns at a tiny fire. When it is your turn to sleep, you find {he} has put {his} own coat over you. When it is {his} turn, {he} does not sleep at all. {He} sits and watches the fire, and sometimes, you think, watches you.

mem.note: gave my coat back at the fire in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} takes it without a word. In the morning you find it over you again.

choices.text: Pretend to sleep, and keep it

mem.note: slept under my coat in the secret realm

effects.log: The coat smells of woodsmoke and of {npc}. You sleep better than you have in years.

events.text: {npc} came into {sr_realm} with you because neither of you would let the other go in alone and come out ahead. Now, at the first real danger, {he} puts {his} back to yours without being asked, and you fight like two people who have studied each other for years. Which you have.

mem.note: fought back to back with me in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} snorts, but {he} does not deny it. For the rest of the road you walk side by side.

mem.note: kept score even in the secret realm

effects.log: You count your kills aloud. So does {he}. You argue about the total all the way to the next ridge.

events.text: On the beast road something huge comes out of the dark at you both, and {npc} shoves you aside and takes the blow on {his} own shoulder. It is over in a moment. Afterwards {he} sits against a tree, pale, holding the arm, and says it is nothing. It is not nothing.

mem.note: bound my arm on the beast road of the secret realm

ok.log: Your bandage holds. {He} flexes {his} fingers and nods, and you both pretend not to be shaken.

mem.note: tried to bind my arm in the secret realm

fail.log: Your bandage slips twice. {He} finishes it with {his} teeth and laughs at you.

mem.note: took the lead on the beast road after I was hurt

effects.log: You go first for the rest of the road and take the next blow yourself. Fair is fair.

events.text: {npc} stares when you turn off the path onto the hidden road as if you had grown up here. 'How do you know the way?' {he} asks. You do not know how to answer. A past life knows the way. You are only following it.

mem.note: told me of a past life on the hidden road

effects.log: {He} listens to the end and does not laugh. Then {he} asks, quietly, whether {he} was there too.

mem.note: lied to me about the hidden road

effects.log: {He} does not believe you, but {he} lets it go, and watches you differently after.

events.text: You and {npc} grew up fighting over everything, and inside {sr_realm} you fight over the map, the water flask, and which of you is in charge. Then something howls in the dark and {he} grabs your sleeve, the way {he} used to when the two of you were children. Neither of you mentions it.

mem.note: held my hand in the dark of the secret realm

effects.log: You hold on until the howling stops. Then you both let go at once and argue about the map again.

mem.note: teased me about the howling in the secret realm

effects.log: At the next fire you bring it up. {He} throws a pinecone at you. It is the most normal thing that has happened all day.

events.text: {npc} watches you find your way through {sr_realm} without a single wrong turn and finally says it. 'You have been here before.' Not a question. Kin know these things. 'Not in this life,' you say, and {he} only nods, as if it explains a great deal about you.

mem.note: told me about a past life in the secret realm

effects.log: It is not much: a smell, a turning, a fear. {He} listens to all of it, and keeps it.

mem.note: kept a past life to {him}self in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} lets you. {He} always has.

events.text: {npc} insisted on coming into {sr_realm} with you, and you are glad of it now, at the fire, under the realm's strange stars. {He} is cleaning your blade without being asked, the way {he} does at home. Out here the small habit feels like a promise.

mem.note: cleaned my blade by the fire in the secret realm

effects.log: You clean {his} blade instead. Neither of you says anything. Neither of you needs to.

mem.note: kept watch while I cleaned the blades in the secret realm

effects.log: You sit with your back to {his} and watch the dark. Nothing comes near the fire all night.

events.text: On the beast road {npc} walks a step ahead of you everywhere, blade out, turning at every sound. When you say {he} does not have to guard you, {he} only says, 'I know.' And keeps doing it.

mem.note: walked beside me on the beast road

effects.log: You take the step that puts you level. {He} sighs, and lets you, and the road is no safer and much better.

mem.note: let me guard the road in the secret realm

effects.log: You let {him}. Some people need to be the wall. You will be {his} another day.

events.text: {npc} is in a secret realm for the first time and keeps forgetting to be afraid, stopping to stare at everything: the light, the strange plants, the bones. You find yourself teaching as you walk, pointing out the tracks, the traps, the places not to step.

mem.note: taught me to read the ground in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} learns fast. By evening {he} is pointing out the traps before you do, and is insufferable about it.

choices.text: Tell {him} to keep close and quiet

mem.note: kept me close in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} sulks, and keeps close, and is alive at the end of the road, which is the point.

events.text: Your disciple {npc} sees before you do that the guardian of {sr_realm} is far beyond you both. {He} says nothing. {He} only takes your sleeve at the next fork and steers you, very politely, toward the longer and safer road.

mem.note: let me steer us away from the guardian

effects.log: You let yourself be steered. A disciple who can tell when the teacher is outmatched is a disciple worth having.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and go your own way

mem.note: would not listen to me in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} follows you without a word, white-faced. You are not sure whether you have taught {him} courage or foolishness.

events.text: At the closing gate {npc} takes the find out of your pack while you are watching for an ambush that never comes, and is three steps away before you understand. {He} does not run. {He} turns and looks at you, and {his} face is the worst of it: not ashamed, only sorry it had to be you.

mem.note: took the find from me at the gate of the secret realm

effects.log: {He} says something about debts, about a chance that comes once. Then the mist closes between you.

mem.note: robbed me at the gate of the secret realm and heard my oath

effects.log: You say it quietly. {He} hears it. That is enough, for now.

mem.note: was let go after robbing me at the gate

effects.log: "Take it," you say. {He} stares at you as if that were the cruellest thing you could have done.

events.text: {npc} has been your friend for years. At the gate of {sr_realm}, with the find in your hands and the mist closing, {he} strikes you behind the ear, takes it, and goes. When you come to, your water flask stands beside your head, carefully upright. Even now {he} could not leave you with nothing.

mem.note: struck me down at the gate of the secret realm and took the find

effects.log: It is the last thing {he} will ever give you, and you hate that it helps.

mem.note: struck me down at the gate of the secret realm

effects.log: It breaks on a stone. You feel no better at all.

events.text: {npc} takes your hand at the gate of {sr_realm}, warm and steady, and while you are holding it, {his} other hand is in your pack. You feel the weight go. You feel {his} fingers tighten on yours, once, like an apology. Then {he} lets go and is gone into the crowd.

mem.note: took the find while holding my hand at the gate

effects.log: You do not call out. You stand there with your hand still warm until the gate has closed.

mem.note: robbed me at the gate, and I shouted after {him}

effects.log: The crowd turns. {npc} does not. The name sounds strange in your mouth now.

events.text: {npc} grabs the find from your hands at the gate of {sr_realm} and runs into the mist, and you stand there with your hands still cupped. Kin. Of all the people who might have done it. Behind you a guard asks if you know that one, and you hear yourself say no.

mem.note: denied me at the gate after I took the find

effects.log: The guard shrugs and turns away. The word stays in your mouth like a stone.

choices.text: Go home and tell no one

mem.note: kept quiet about what I did at the gate

effects.log: You carry it inside you. Kin have survived worse, people say. You hope they are right.

events.text: {npc} is gone when you wake on the last morning in {sr_realm}, and so is the find. There is a note in {his} hand under a stone. {He} is sorry, it says; the debt is larger than you know; {he} will explain. It does not say when.

mem.note: left a note when I took the find from the secret realm

effects.log: You fold it small and keep it. Some day {he} will explain, and you want to have it in your hand when {he} does.

mem.note: took the find and left only a note

effects.log: It goes up quickly. The words are still there when you close your eyes.

events.text: Your own disciple {npc} takes the find from your pack at the gate of {sr_realm}, and when you catch {his} wrist {he} twists free with a move you taught {him} last spring. {He} is through the mist before you can follow. You taught {him} that move well. That is the part you cannot stop thinking about.

mem.note: was disowned for taking the find at the gate

effects.log: You strike the name from your teaching roll that night. The ink takes a long time to dry.

mem.note: took the find at the gate, and found the door left open

effects.log: Some disciples come back. You leave the door unbarred, and do not let yourself watch it.

events.text: Of course {npc} is here. You see {him} across a clearing in {sr_realm}, as you always see {him}, at the worst moment: just as you reach for a find in the roots of a fallen tree. {He} sees it too. You both stop. You were born the same night. You know how this goes.

mem.note: beat me to a find in the secret realm

ok.log: You reach the roots first, and hold them. {He} wipes {his} mouth, nods, and goes. Next time, the nod says.

mem.note: lost a find to me in the secret realm

fail.log: {He} is a breath faster. {He} holds up the find, salutes you with it, and is gone into the trees.

mem.note: let me take a find in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} hesitates, suspicious, then takes it. At the edge of the clearing {he} looks back, as if trying to work out what you have won.

mem.note: outran me to a find in the secret realm

ok.log: You are over the trunk and gone before {he} moves. {His} curse follows you a long way.

mem.note: lost a race to me in the secret realm

fail.log: {He} is there first, laughing, the find held over {his} head.

events.text: {npc} finds you at a spring deep in {sr_realm} and sits down on the other side of it without a word. After a while {he} says, 'Last life we came in here together too. You went left at the bones. I went right.' You do not remember. But your feet, earlier today, went left at the bones.

choices.text: Ask what happened to {him} on the right

mem.note: listened to what the right-hand road cost me

effects.log: {He} tells you. It is a long story, and not a happy one, and at the end {he} looks at you as if you owed {him} something. Perhaps you do.

mem.note: pretended to remember the realm

effects.log: {He} knows you are lying. {He} smiles anyway, and fills {his} flask, and goes.

events.text: In the narrowest place in {sr_realm}, where a rope bridge spans a drop into mist, {npc} waits on the far side with a knife against the ropes. 'I could,' {he} says. 'You know I could.' The bridge sways under your feet. It would look like an accident. Everyone dies in the secret realms.

mem.note: walked my bridge without flinching

effects.log: You cross the whole bridge with your eyes on {him}. {He} does not cut. When you reach {him}, {he} puts the knife away and says, "Not like this."

choices.text: Turn back and find another way

effects.log: You hear {him} laugh across the mist. It costs you half a day, and you are alive.

mem.note: charged me on the bridge in the secret realm

ok.log: You cross at a run and are on {him} before {he} can cut. {He} goes over backwards into the moss and laughs up at you.

mem.note: made me cross on one rope

fail.log: {He} cuts one rope, only one. You cross the last stretch hand over hand, swinging, while {he} watches.

events.text: {npc} is hurt. You find {him} against a wall in {sr_realm} with a twisted leg and {his} sword out of reach, and the sound of something large coming closer. {He} looks up and sees it is you, and of everything you have ever seen in that face, this is new: relief.

mem.note: carried me out of the secret realm when I was hurt

effects.log: {He} is heavier than {he} looks, swears at you the whole way, and does not let go of your shoulder once.

choices.text: Hand {him} the sword and stand with {him}

mem.note: stood with me against the beast in the secret realm

effects.log: You fight it off together, back to back, the way you never have before.

mem.note: left me hurt in the secret realm

effects.log: You walk away. The sounds behind you go on a long time. {He} lives; you learn that later. {He} never forgets.

events.text: You are a mile down the hidden road when footsteps sound behind you, and you turn to find {npc}, out of breath and grinning. 'I knew it,' {he} says. 'I knew you would know a way. I have followed you since the gate.'

mem.note: shared the hidden road with me

effects.log: You walk the hidden road together. {He} knows each turn a breath after you do, as if reading them off your back.

mem.note: lost me in the dark of the hidden road

ok.log: You double back twice and leave {him} cursing in a dead end.

mem.note: could not shake me off the hidden road

fail.log: {He} is still behind you at the end, grinning wider.

events.text: {npc} stands on a ridge above you in {sr_realm}, the whole realm spread out below. {He} has grown since you last met; you can see it in the way {he} stands. 'Once in sixty years,' {he} calls down. 'Whoever comes out with the great find is the one the world remembers. Shall we settle it here?'

mem.note: beat me on the ridge of the great realm

ok.log: You meet on the ridge. When it is over {he} is on one knee, and the realm, it seems, has watched.

mem.note: lost to me on the ridge of the great realm

fail.log: {He} wins, cleanly, and walks off toward the guardian without looking back.

choices.text: Say the realm is bigger than both of you

mem.note: would not fight me with the great realm at our feet

effects.log: {He} looks at the realm below, then at you, and laughs. "Fine," {he} says. "After."

events.text: {npc} is in {sr_realm} too, and for once it is a relief. The two of you have made your peace, and now you walk the realm side by side like old comrades. {He} points out a trap you missed. You pull {him} back from a ledge. Neither of you keeps score any more. It is strange how much lighter that is.

mem.note: shared the find in the secret realm

effects.log: You split it on a flat rock, exactly in half. {He} pushes {his} half back toward you, and you push it back again.

choices.text: Race {him} to the next ridge, for fun

mem.note: beat me to the ridge, for fun

ok.log: You win by a stride. {He} pretends to be furious. Neither of you believes it.

mem.note: raced me to the ridge, for fun

fail.log: {He} wins by a stride and does not let you forget it for the rest of the day.

events.text: {npc} finds you standing at the place in {sr_realm} where a past life of yours died. {He} stands beside you, and after a while says quietly, 'I was there. Last time. I did not help you.' {He} does not say sorry. Born the same night, every time: perhaps this is the closest {he} can come.

mem.note: forgave me for the last life in the secret realm

effects.log: {He} nods once, and does not look at you, and walks the rest of the road a step behind you, like a guard.

choices.text: Say you will not wait for {him} this time

mem.note: told me plainly at the place of the old death

effects.log: "Good," {he} says, and means it, and something between you is honest at last.

events.text: {npc} stands at the gate of {sr_realm} in a borrowed travelling coat, too big in the shoulders, trying to look as if {he} is not frightened. You are past the barrier's limit now. All you can do is send {him} in with everything you know, and wait for the season to end.

mem.note: came out of the secret realm with a find, because of what I was taught

ok.log: {npc} comes out at the season's end thinner and browner and grinning, with a pouch of spirit stones and a story {he} will tell for the rest of {his} life.

mem.note: came back hurt from the secret realm I was sent into

fail.log: {npc} comes out at the season's end on a stretcher, with a broken arm and a long scar on {his} jaw. {He} found nothing. {He} is alive. You hold on to that.

choices.text: Give {him} your old blade and your blessing

mem.note: carried my elder's blade through the secret realm

ok.log: The blade comes back notched, with {npc} behind it, and {his} first real find tied to the hilt.

mem.note: broke the blade I was given in the secret realm

fail.log: {npc} limps out at the end with your blade in two pieces and {his} pride in more. {He} will heal. The blade will not.

events.text: The night before {sr_realm} opens, {npc} sits by your door sharpening a knife that does not need sharpening. 'Will I come back?' {he} asks, without looking up. Kin ask the questions nobody else will.

mem.note: was promised I would come back, and did

ok.log: The promise holds. {npc} comes back with dirt in {his} hair and a spirit stone in each fist, and throws them at you laughing.

mem.note: came back hurt from the secret realm despite the promise

fail.log: {npc} comes back, as you promised. Hurt, which you did not. {He} does not hold it against you. You do.

mem.note: was told the truth before the secret realm

ok.log: The truth makes {him} careful. {npc} comes out with a find and not a scratch.

mem.note: came back hurt and empty-handed from the secret realm

fail.log: The truth makes {him} afraid, and fear makes {him} slow. {He} comes out bruised and empty-handed.

events.text: {npc} is grown and strong and more than ready for {sr_realm}, and when you say you will send {him} in, {he} only nods, as if {he} has been waiting for you to ask. At the gate {he} turns once, raises a hand, and is gone into the mist.

choices.text: Wait at the gate all season

mem.note: came out to find my elder waiting at the gate

ok.log: You see {him} first, out of the mist at the season's end, a find held high so you can see it from the crowd.

mem.note: came out of the secret realm hurt

fail.log: You see {him} first, out of the mist at the season's end, leaning on a stranger's shoulder. Hurt. Home.

mem.note: was trusted to go into the secret realm alone

ok.log: {npc} walks in through your door at the season's end and sets a spirit stone on the table without a word. That is how {he} tells it.

mem.note: came home hurt from the secret realm

fail.log: {npc} comes home at the season's end with bandages on both hands. {He} does not want to talk about it, and you do not make {him}.

events.text: {npc} comes out of {sr_realm} with a find and a new friend from a rival house, and by the end of the month {he} has sold the find to that house, and the house has used it against yours. {He} says {he} did not know. {He} looks at the floor while {he} says it.

mem.note: was forgiven for selling the find of the secret realm

effects.log: {He} cries, which {he} has not done since {he} was small. It does not undo anything. It is a start.

mem.note: was punished for selling the find of the secret realm

effects.log: A season of hard work and no allowance. {He} does it without complaint, and does not meet your eyes until spring.

mem.note: had to show what the find of the secret realm was sold for

effects.log: {He} empties the purse on the table. It is not much. That is almost the worst of it.

events.text: The gate of {sr_realm} closes at the season's end, and you stand at it with the other families until the last of the mist is gone. {npc} does not come out. Nobody saw {him} after the guardian's hall. A stranger who was there brings you {his} travelling coat, folded very neatly.

choices.text: Wait at the gate another day

effects.log: You wait. Then another day. The barrier will not open again for years, and you know it, and you wait.
You carry it home. You do not unfold it. Not that year, nor for many after.

events.text: Your disciple {npc} kneels before you on the morning {sr_realm} opens, asking leave to go in. You are past the barrier's limit; {he} is not. You give {him} a map drawn from memory and three rules, and watch {him} walk into the mist with your teaching on {his} back.

mem.note: came back from the secret realm with a find, by the three rules

ok.log: {npc} comes back with the rules intact, a find in {his} sleeve, and the look of a fighter who has stepped up a realm in a season.

mem.note: forgot a rule in the secret realm and was hurt

fail.log: {npc} forgot the second rule at the worst moment. {He} comes back hurt, and ashamed, and asks to be taught the rules again.

mem.note: was saved in the secret realm by the talisman I was given

ok.log: The talisman comes back cracked down the middle. It took a blow meant for {him}. {npc} brings it back with a find, and both hands shaking.

mem.note: came back hurt from the secret realm

fail.log: The talisman did nothing. {npc} comes out bandaged and empty-handed and very quiet.

events.text: {npc} has trained a year for {sr_realm}, and the whole school knows it. On the day, the juniors line the road to see {him} off. {He} bows to you at the barrier, very formally, and then, suddenly young, grins.

mem.note: was seen off with honour and came back with a find

ok.log: The juniors cheer. {npc} goes in proud, and comes out prouder, with a find to lay at your feet.

mem.note: came back from the secret realm on a stretcher

fail.log: The juniors cheer. {npc} comes out at the season's end on a stretcher, and the cheering is very quiet this time.

mem.note: went into the secret realm laughing, and came out laughing

ok.log: {npc} laughs and goes in light-footed. {He} comes out the same way, with a spirit stone and a new scar {he} is very pleased with.

mem.note: came out of the secret realm limping

fail.log: {npc} goes in light-footed and comes out limping, still grinning, though it costs {him}.

events.text: {npc} comes out of {sr_realm} with the realm's find and does not bring it to you. You hear of it from a merchant: your disciple has taken it to a rival master, along with your teaching, and knelt to a new teacher. The merchant watches your face with interest.

mem.note: left my teacher for another with the find of the secret realm

effects.log: Every teacher loses one. You put away {his} practice sword and do not take it down again.

mem.note: was beaten in the street by the teacher I left

ok.log: You find {him} at the rival master's gate. It is a short fight. {He} hands over the find and will not look at you.

mem.note: beat my old teacher in the street

fail.log: {He} has learned more than you knew. {He} beats you in the street, in front of {his} new master, and bows.

events.text: The gate of {sr_realm} closes, the parties come out one by one, and {npc} is not among them. A disciple from another school saw {him} last at the guardian's door, going in alone. 'Brave,' the stranger says. 'Very brave.' As if it helps.

effects.log: You burn it at the school's gate, where {he} bowed to you. The smoke goes straight up, the way {he} always stood.

choices.text: Go over every lesson you gave {him}

effects.log: Every rule. Every map. Was one of them wrong? You will never know.

events.text: {npc} asks to go into {sr_realm} not for the find, {he} says, but to see what you saw when you were young. Every teacher has a story {his} disciples have heard too often. {npc} wants to know if yours is true.

choices.text: Tell {him} the story one more time

mem.note: found my teacher's story true in the secret realm

ok.log: {npc} comes out at the season's end and finds you, and says only, "It was true." Then {he} gives you a spirit stone, as if paying for the story.

mem.note: found the worst part the story left out

fail.log: {npc} comes out hurt and finds you anyway. "The story left out the worst part," {he} says, and you have to admit it did.

mem.note: was told to find my own story in the secret realm

ok.log: {He} does. It is better than yours, and {he} brings back a find to prove it.

mem.note: came back from the secret realm with a broken rib

fail.log: {His} own story has a broken rib in it. {He} tells it to you anyway, wincing, very proud.

events.text: Years after you came out of the secret realm, you still dream of it some nights: the light, the air, the guardian's eyes. You wake with your hand on your blade and the smell of another world in your nose. The dreams are not nightmares, exactly. They feel more like an invitation.

effects.log: You train until dawn. The dream fades. The invitation does not.
You fill three pages. Reading them back in daylight, you find a thing you did not know you had noticed.

events.text: A young fighter turns up at your door with a cheap map of a secret realm and a hundred questions. Someone in the tavern said you went in and came out. They want to know what to take, what to fear, and which road to choose.

effects.log: You talk until the lamp gutters. They leave with a full head and an empty map, and you feel strangely light.
They will go anyway. They always do. But they will remember you said it, at the worst moment, and perhaps it will save them.

events.text: Years later you still check your pack when a friend stands too close. You still sleep with your back to a wall when you travel with company. The one who turned on you at the realm's gate is far away now, or dead, or forgiven; it hardly matters. What they took was never really the find.

effects.log: You let a friend carry your pack for a day. Nothing happens. It is the hardest day's walk of your life.
A guard kept is a guard you will not need to find in a hurry. You keep it.

events.text: A junior disciple of your sect breaks through to a new realm on a pill made from the find you gave up at the gate of a secret realm, years ago. Nobody tells the junior where the pill came from. You watch the celebration from the back of the hall and find you do not mind at all.

effects.log: The junior stares, then bows so low it is almost comic. You have a devoted follower now, whether you want one or not.
Some gifts are better unsigned. You slip out before the speeches.

events.text: A broad man in an iron-ringed coat finds you on the road, years after the Valley of a Hundred Beasts, and offers enough silver for a house for the beast core you carried out. Iron-Net Gwak. He has been looking for you. You remember a young woman's hand on your sleeve at the gate, and a promise.

effects.log: You tell him no. He names a bigger number. You tell him no again, and he goes off puzzled, as people like him always are by a promise.
He counts the silver out on a tree stump. You do not look at the core as he takes it.

events.text: A young man with a farm accent stops you in the market and bows so low that people stare. 'Pyo Dal-i,' he says. 'My mother says you gave her your flask at the gate of the Spirit Spring. I had a cough that would not stop. Look at me now.' He is broad and tall and laughing, and he has brought you a basket of eggs.

effects.log: They are very good eggs. You eat one standing in the market, and he laughs again, delighted.
She is old now, he says, and still talks about the spring, and about you.

events.text: A book comes out in the capital: 'The Sect That Burned Its Name', by the late historian Yeo Seon-u. On the last page are two characters, and a line of thanks to a stranger who carried a rubbing out of the ruins. Scholars argue over it in the teahouses. Some say the name should never have been printed.

effects.log: You read it in one night. He wrote you in as "a traveller of few words", which is fair.
Somewhere on that mountain a grey disciple still keeps a door. You hope it does not mind.

events.text: In a market far from any bamboo you hear three notes, a pause, three notes. Eun Sol sits on a mat by the well with his flute, older now, playing the Labyrinth's tune for coppers. He stops when your shadow falls across his bowl. 'I know that step,' he says, and smiles at a point just past your shoulder.

effects.log: He plays the whole form for you. Halfway through, your hand starts moving on your knee, cutting air.
He hears the weight of it and raises an eyebrow. "Too much," he says. You leave it anyway.

events.text: A river village you have never visited sends you a gift: a carved wooden tiger with a grin, and a letter in a careful hand. The Heo house paid for a new well and a school, it says, and Heo Ran said to thank you, because it was your idea. The school is named for the Bandit King.

effects.log: The children of the school sing you the Bandit King's three laws. They have added a fourth: Share the find.

choices.text: Keep the tiger on your desk

effects.log: It grins at you every morning. You find you grin back.

events.text: Sometimes, years after the great secret realm, you catch yourself holding your hands the way you held them before its guardian, and the world goes very quiet around you. Once in sixty years. You were there, and you won, and some part of you never quite came out.

effects.log: You sit in it on purpose for an hour. Something in your cultivation shifts, very slightly, like a key half turned.
You laugh, roll your shoulders, and go and find something loud to do.

events.text: A guardian of a secret realm still visits you, years later, in small ways: a sound in the trees that is almost a footstep, a breath of wind that is almost a blade. You beat it once. You are not sure, any more, whether it lost, or let you pass.

effects.log: It is a humbler thought, and a kinder one. You sleep well that night.
You did. You have the find to prove it, or had. You stand a little straighter.
